body:
I don't follow why this should be treated as a presentational attribute. They sound like very different things to me.

The attribute does help author convenience, but it doesn't come at the cost of other problems. If we compare it with the ["a number of problems" of presentational markup](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/introduction.html#presentational-markup):
- Accessibility:
  -  An element and its anchor (eg about a popover and its button) are often semantically connected. The attribute adds more semantics to the element
  - The attribute is also media independent
- Maintenance cost: This reduces maintenance cost. This allows reusing the same style for positioning different elements that have different anchors
- Document size: This reduces document size as the result of reusing style

On the other hand, presentational attributes are often (if not always) equivalent to adding some style rules to the element (eg `<ol type="I">` is equivalent to adding `list-style-type: upper-roman`). And they got overridden by any style rule of a higher precendence.

The `anchor` attribute doesn't add any style rule, and the implicit anchor element won't be overridden by any style rule. It simply adds an entry point to the "implicit anchor element" concept, which is intentionally left open in the anchor positioning spec for other specs to work with.

> I usually think of presentational attributes as redundant with style="". Is that the case here?

No. There's no way (and won't be any way) for any style rule (regardless in `style=""`, `<style>` or external style sheet) to override the implicit anchor element.
